messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] High p99 latency and increased 5xx for /v1/generate — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s, p99 ~2.4s. Error rate increased 0.2% -> 9.3%. Canary release a92f deployed ~10m ago. Grafana: <link> | Trace samples: trace/8f3a, trace/9b2c.
Diego (oncall): I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime and eng-platform. tagging @Alice @Ben.
Alice (eng-runtime): looking at runtime traces now. KV-cache miss rate spiked on redis-shard-3; lots of long latency in kv fetch (200-800ms). Collecting logs.
Ben (eng-platform): canary hosts show huge tail, but non-canary prod nodes less affected. That suggests release-induced behavior in some host configs.
Clara (product): any immediate customer impact? Maya, are we seeing inbound tickets?
Maya (support): Yep — support queue volume up 6x for EU customers, several reports of 502s/timeouts. A couple of enterprise customers seeing retries spike.
Diego (oncall): propose immediate rollback of canary a92f and pause rollout. If rollback doesn't restore, we'll cut region traffic. Opinions?
Alice (eng-runtime): Agreed. Rolling back canary first. Command:
```
/ops/releases rollback --release=a92f --scope=canary --region=eu-west
```
Alice (eng-runtime): rollback kicked off at 1765432180.
IncidentBot: Rollback action submitted by Alice at 1765432180. Change ID: rollback-1765432180.
Ben (eng-platform): Confirmed rollback completed on 2/3 canary hosts at 1765432205; third host finishing. Watching metrics.
Alice (eng-runtime): p99 on canaries dropped to ~140ms within 90s. Error rate on those hosts down to ~0.8%. Gateway still reporting some 502s from edge -> investigating proxy/connection resets.
Raj (infra): I'm seeing increased connection resets from edge to backend pool around 1765432145. Kernel TCP keepalive/ephemeral sockets hitting limits on proxy pool. Raised keepalive and bumped backend connection pool. Also enabled stricter circuit-breaker on backend service to stop cascading failures.
Diego (oncall): Good. Start P1 incident. Clara, Maya — please draft customer comms and update status page. Zoe, ping top customers.
Clara (product): Drafting status update: "Degraded performance for generation API (EU-west). We identified a canary release and are rolling back; mitigation in progress." Will post once approved.
Maya (support): DM'ing Zoe with list of affected accounts and draft outreach. Putting high-touch list into support queue.
Ben (eng-platform): Short-term mitigation idea: route 10% of traffic to fallback model variant (v-small) to reduce pressure while we stabilize. Applying traffic rule now: /ops/traffic set-weight generate:v-small=10% region=eu-west
Alice (eng-runtime): Fallback routing applied at 1765432260. Queue depth falling, observing lower tail latencies on backend.
Diego (oncall): Handing off to Ben for monitoring and follow-through in 25 minutes. I'll stay on-call for escalation. Assign postmortem owner — Alice?
Ben (eng-platform): I'll take immediate follow-up. Paused full rollout and removed a92f from remaining rollout queue.
Alice (eng-runtime): Adding debug snippets to incident ticket: latest logs show Redis GET latency spikes correlated with mem-eviction events; possible regression in new serialization path in a92f.
Maya (support): Posted preliminary note to status page at 1765432300. Message: "We are experiencing degraded performance for generation API in EU-west. Engineers are investigating; a rollback is in progress."
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-17654321, severity P1. Pager escalations enabled; channel linked.
Raj (infra): Observed residual 502s due to queued requests hitting proxy timeouts during rollback window. Increasing proxy timeout & enabling backoff on retryer. Should drop error rate further.
Ben (eng-platform): p99 across region now ~170ms, total error rate ~0.6% (5m window). Keeping fallback routing in place until postmortem.
Zoe (customer-success): Notifying accounts team: will start personal outreach for top 5 customers within 30m.
Diego (oncall): Last check at 1765432420 — p99 170ms, error 0.6%. Moving to monitoring state. Handoff complete to Ben. Postmortem owner: Alice.
Ben (eng-platform): Next steps: root-cause triage focused on serialization path and redis interactions introduced in a92f; postmortem to include timeline, rollout gating improvements, and canary rollback automation review.
Clara (product): We'll schedule customer follow-ups + postmortem readout.
All: reactions — :thumbsup: to those on rollback and outreach.
Diego (oncall): closing thread for now, will re-open if metrics regress.
